title: Commit to a public extension platform with persistent permissions
decision: Choose whether to make a two-year compatibility commitment for a third-party extension platform with persistent local permissions in the next release.
options: Launch the public extension platform and compatibility promise now
Ship two internal adapters while keeping the interface private
Reject the platform direction for the current product horizon

evidence.content: Three named design partners have each committed engineering time to a different extension and require a stable public interface before starting.
A bounded prototype with two private adapters increased activated workflows from 18 of 100 to 41 of 100 in the target cohort.
Persistent extension permissions introduce privilege persistence, confused-deputy, revocation, supply-chain, and data-exfiltration failure paths that do not exist in the private-adapter design.
The two-year promise consumes an estimated 30 percent of the maintainer's roadmap capacity and makes permission-model changes costly for all adopters.
Once external extensions persist user data, rollback requires migration and revocation support rather than a simple feature disable.
